arguments.description: Small boxy robot sprite: a dark navy rectangular frame with two rectangular antenna posts rising from its top corners, a flat teal front panel, and two rectangular pale-yellow eyes. Flat eye-level pixel art in three colours (navy, teal, pale yellow) on a transparent background, no shading or outline gradients. Rotate this exact sprite; keep its height, width, colours, silhouette and simple box volume in every view.

choices.choice: create_object_pro_flash with the exact source as first_frame_url and n_directions=8
choices.reason: Cheapest discovered route (rotations only, quoted 1 generation) that takes the actual pixels as the south frame without a humanoid skeleton assumption; the robot is a limbless box, which create_character v3 documents as a body it 'tends to add limbs' to. Fallbacks ranked in discovery-01.json.

The source is drawn strictly frontal with no visible top face; an eye-level camera keeps the preserved south consistent with the generated views. 'low top-down' would invent a top surface the south frame does not have. Open to caller correction if the game camera is known to be top-down.
East/north/west are only available through the 8-view rotation; the four diagonals are retained but not delivered.
Reproducibility of the attempt record; a revision would use a different seed.
Matches the source (0 fractional pixels) and nearest sampling; proposal, not an owner rule.

choices.choice: One sample-phase generation task (plar_prepare) proves the method; accepted bytes are then reused as production-stage members under a family delivery with the preserved south as baseline; no second paid call unless a revision is needed
choices.reason: PX2 family members must be production outputs sharing a sample baseline; the representative sample supplies the adoption proof.

choices.choice: Continuity, direction mapping and renderer (engine) checks are family-level, reviewed after all four files exist
choices.reason: They cannot pass on a single direction; deferral keeps the obligation scheduled rather than dropped.

Caller correction 1: the declared schema says every drawn pixel is one of them and supplied pixels stay as they are, enforcing the owner palette requirement at generation. Deterministic palette/alpha correction remains a fallback, recorded as an 'edited' member distinct from raw provider bytes.

excerpts.text:
## Useful assignment: complete missing robot directions

The existing examples/delegation consumer has an approved identity fixture and
missing directional files. This later CF-10 addendum explicitly authorizes actual
official production, superseding only the old BRIEF.md plan-only/no-runner scope.
Keep the original brief, controller, source image and original plar.txt unchanged.
The old approval is within this representative fixture, not a real-game art claim.

Select robot.directions from production-plar.txt, including robot.base's identity reference.
Inspect assets/robot-base.png first. Preserve its exact south PNG bytes as
assets/robot/south.png. Use the actual source pixels as the provider's existing
identity/south input, not a filename in a text description or a redesigned robot.
Generate the useful missing east, north and west views, separate transparent
32x32 PNGs at the controller's exact assets/robot/<direction>.png paths.
Inspect subject identity, proportions, palette, volume, direction and anchor/alignment
at native size and 3x nearest. Extra returned directions may be retained but are
not required delivered work. Do not regenerate the approved south for counts.

Use fresh .pixl/assets/robot.directions with ordinary public plan/job/review/family
operations. Multi-output plans require an explicit family delivery output/link;
do not declare the first single direction to satisfy the whole assigned family.
The bounded renderer-native/ imports actual src/robot.ts and observes all four
controller states. Run the copied renderer with these consumer-root paths:
`node renderer-native/capture.mjs --project . --out work/native-production/render-01`
`"C:/github/pixel-lab-agent/build/readiness-setup-01/runtime/Scripts/python.exe" renderer-native/check.py --project . --capture work/native-production/render-01 --out work/native-production/renderer-check-01.json`
Read renderer-native/README.md for its contract. Save exact returned reports and
inspect destination.png and all actual 1x/3x cells
with the host image tool. It is a supporting CF-10 renderer, not broad TM-08 or
game-engine qualification. Current acceptance requires actual visual judgment.

## Scope, payment and source authority

requirements.name: dims
requirements.check: The file is a 32x32 RGBA PNG (one frame).

requirements.name: alpha_transparent
requirements.check: Every pixel outside the robot has alpha 0, the robot has at least one opaque pixel, and there is no opaque matte, backdrop or canvas fill behind it.

requirements.name: alpha_binary
requirements.check: No pixel has fractional alpha: every alpha value is 0 or 255.

requirements.name: palette_preserved
requirements.check: Every opaque pixel is one of the source's three colours #25354a, #56b5bc, #f4dda2; no new colours are introduced.

requirements.name: identity
requirements.check: Viewed at 1x and 3x nearest, the sprite reads as the same robot as assets/robot-base.png: a dark navy rectangular frame with two square antenna posts on top and a teal body panel, with the pale-yellow rectangular eyes wherever the facing shows the front. No added limbs, wheels, extra faces, text or other features, and no redesign.

requirements.name: proportions_volume
requirements.check: The sprite keeps the source's height (antenna tops about row 3, base about row 27, 25 px tall, within 1 px) and reads as the same simple box volume turned to the named facing; it is not stretched, shrunk, squashed or re-proportioned, and the antennae keep their post size.

requirements.name: direction
requirements.check: The sprite faces the viewer's right (east): the front/eye panel is turned toward the right edge or seen in right profile. It is not the south frame copied, and it is not another facing mislabelled.

requirements.name: anchor_alignment
requirements.check: Shown in the same 32x32 cell as the south frame (1x and 3x), the sprite stands on the same ground line and is centred like the source, so swapping facings in the controller does not visibly jump or float.

requirements.name: ground_line_measure
requirements.check: Measured on the visible bounding box (zero-based, exclusive bottom/right): bottom == 28 (last opaque row 27, as the source) and |(left + right) / 2 - 16| <= 1 (source box [7,25) has centre 16).
